title: DuRTL - Information Flow Analysis Tool for Register Transfer Level Hardware Designs
problem: Understanding and comprehending unknown or legacy hardware designs written in Verilog/VHDL is challenging. Information flow tracking is critical for security analysis, verification, and design understanding but lacks accessible tools.
motivation: Open-source hardware information flow analysis tool enables designers to understand unknown designs by tracking how information propagates through circuits, identifying data dependencies and potential information leakage paths.
method: DuRTL implements Hardware Information Flow Tracking (IFT) using tagging mechanism. Unique tags injected into hardware designs; each tag associates a signal at a specific time with information flow during circuit traversal.
key_novelty: Open-source C++ tool for RTL-level information flow analysis supporting Verilog and VHDL, enabling automated tracking of information propagation through unknown hardware designs.
contributions: Open-source DuRTL information flow analysis tool
limitations: Tool paper with abstract only; specific experimental results and benchmarks not detailed; scalability characteristics not discussed; no comparison with other IFT tools.
primary_theme: Hardware design analysis and verification tools
